headline: Revenue ticks up, but profitability slips as GTA VI nears
summary_short: GAAP net revenue rose 2.0% y/y to $1,533.9M even as Net Bookings — Take-Two's operating metric — fell 3% to $1.39B, and the GAAP net loss widened to $34.1M ($0.18/share) from $11.9M ($0.07/share) a year ago on a $43.4M cost-of-revenue impairment tied to a canceled third-party title.
summary_long: GAAP revenue rose 2.0% y/y to $1,533.9M — console net revenue grew 16% while mobile and PC net revenue each declined — but Net Bookings, the company's point-of-sale operating metric, fell 3% to $1.39B, slightly above its own guidance range, ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI's November 19 launch. Cost of revenue absorbed a $43.4M impairment on a canceled third-party title, driving the GAAP net loss to $34.1M ($0.18/share) from $11.9M ($0.07/share) a year ago; company-defined EBITDA fell 25.9% y/y to $167.0M. Cash and short-term investments fell to $1,826.6M from $1,989.3M at fiscal year-end as operating activities used $168.8M of cash. Management reiterated FY2027 Net Bookings guidance of $8.0-$8.2B and issued initial fiscal-Q2 guidance of $1.62-$1.67B.

drivers.explanation: GAAP revenue recognizes $148.0M of previously deferred revenue this quarter, per the company's own GAAP-to-management reconciliation table, which is why revenue rose 2% y/y even as Net Bookings — the point-of-sale operating metric — fell 3%.
EPS fell alongside net income on the $43.4M cost-of-revenue impairment charge; per-share loss widened further because weighted average shares rose 3% y/y to 186.2M from 180.8M, diluting the loss.

GAAP net loss widened to $34.1M from $11.9M a year ago, driven by a $43.4M cost-of-revenue impairment charge tied to the Company's decision not to proceed with an unannounced third-party-developed title.
Cost of revenue absorbed the same $43.4M impairment charge that drove the net loss, pushing gross profit down 6.6% y/y despite the 2% revenue increase.
Operating income swung to a $35.5M loss from $21.6M income a year ago, primarily reflecting the $43.4M cost-of-revenue impairment charge on the canceled third-party title.

Per the release's own reconciliation (net loss adjusted for tax benefit, net interest, depreciation, and $160.5M of acquired-intangible amortization), EBITDA fell 25.9% y/y to $167.0M, tracking the same impairment-driven operating decline.
Cash fell to $1,364.9M from $1,545.5M at fiscal year-end as operating activities used $168.8M of cash this quarter, versus $44.7M used a year ago; the release does not itemize the swing further.

Long-term debt fell $598.2M q/q while short-term debt rose $599.9M q/q — a near-exact offset suggesting reclassification of near-maturity debt to current rather than repayment; the release does not explain the shift.

CEO Zelnick called the quarter's results 'excellent' and reiterated FY2027 Net Bookings guidance of $8.0-8.2B ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI's November 19th launch; the release gives no further operational driver detail beyond segment tables and the one-time impairment.
